Known only from a search summary; primary source not opened.

No referee or named expert verification after seven years; hypotheses changed substantially between versions (GCH + measurable dropped); only engagement is an unverified forum remark that it is not independently checked.
The L_{ω1,ω} reduction is a one-paragraph cited step, not checked; the uniform theorem it rests on is unreviewed; Lean formalisation covers only the AEC CH obstruction, not the L_{ω1,ω} corollary.
events.ai_basis: The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model.

why: The statement fixes the threshold as the Hanf number of L_{ω1,ω}. Every event either works in a different setting (AECs, universal classes, L_{κ,ω} with large cardinals, atomic classes), uses a different threshold or hypothesis form, or concerns a different namesake conjecture. All of these are variants or none. The close call is openai-math-240. Its corollary covers countable-vocabulary L_{ω1,ω} sentences with an unspecified threshold μ(ℵ₀), and the manuscript itself says the prescribed ℶ_{ω1} threshold 'remains a separate question'. Showing that categoricity transfers above some cardinal is the eventual-categoricity form, a weaker statement than one at the Hanf number, so it is a variant rather than a case. Its CH obstruction is about general AECs at ℶ_{ω2}, and the record says it is not claimed to be L_{ω1,ω}-definable, so it is neither a counterexample to nor a case of this statement. Vasey's universal-sentence theorems were judged variants rather than cases because their threshold (ℶ_{ℶ_{ω1}}) or hypothesis form (an end segment below ℶ_ω) differs from the statement's. They predate the snapshot and are not whole in any case. Espíndola's result has its own threshold and exceptional cardinals and is unrefereed, so it is likewise a variant. The AI credit for openai-math-240 comes from a README-wide quote, not one specific to this family.
doubts: The ai_role for openai-math-240 rests on a repository-wide README statement ('the vast majority of results'), not on a disclosure specific to this family. A reader could treat Vasey 2016 (universal sentences) as a case with a weaker threshold, but it predates the snapshot and is not whole, so the outcome does not change. Whether Espíndola's θ = ω corollary exactly gives the statement with the ℶ_{ω1} threshold is unresolved in the record.
